en.title: Colors and descriptions
en.goal: Describe colors, objects and people's characteristics.

phrases.scenario: Someone asks your favorite color, which is blue. What do you say?
Someone asks what your new colleague is like, and she is very kind. What do you say?

phrases.t: My cat is black and white.
phrases.scenario: Someone asks what your cat looks like, and it's black and white. What do you answer?
You're describing a pretty red dress you saw in a shop. What do you say?

phrases.t: The sweater is green and yellow.

dialogue.title: Describing someone
lines: He's tall and has black hair.

adjective-placement.title: Why "une jolie robe rouge" and not "une rouge jolie robe"?
adjective-placement.body: Most adjectives in French come after the noun (une robe rouge, un chat noir) — unlike English, where adjectives come before the noun. Only a small group of common, short adjectives (like jolie, grand, petit, bon) come before: une jolie robe. That's why "a pretty red dress" is une jolie robe rouge — jolie before, rouge after.

gentil-sympa.title: In everyday speech, "gentil" often becomes "sympa"
gentil-sympa.body: Notice that the dialogue you just read already uses sympa ("Il est sympa ?") — a very common short form of sympathique, used all the time instead of gentil to say someone is nice / a good person.

bandeira-tricolor-historia.title: Bleu, blanc, rouge — the origin of the French flag
bandeira-tricolor-historia.body: The 3 colors you just learned are those of the French flag: bleu and rouge were the colors of Paris, and blanc was the traditional color of the monarchy — the flag, created during the French Revolution, combines the two.
